what: Mount names written before the six arcs existed, and the arcs each one expands to, held across the language boundary.
why: A fleet file names its arcs as text, and two implementations read that text: ExpandLegacyArc in
InMemoryMatchService.Normalization.cs and expandLegacyArc in normalize.ts. They agreed on every
spelling either suite exercised and disagreed on the one neither did: the server stripped spaces
AND hyphens before comparing, the client stripped only spaces and only in its fallback branch.
So a weapons cell reading `Fore-Port` resolved to ForePort on the server and fell back to Fore on
the client. The mount lost its port arc on screen while the server went on firing it through both
- the two halves of the app describing one ship differently, with nothing to notice.
The cases below are the ones a file can actually carry: the four old ninety-degree names, the
six-arc names spelled the several ways a person writes them, and the blind spot, which no
expansion may ever resurrect because no weapon fires through it. legacyArcCases.test.ts runs
them against the client and LegacyArcParityTests runs the same list against the server, so a
change to either normalizer reddens one of the two suites.
`aft` is the case worth reading twice: as an OLD arc name it was ninety degrees wide and becomes
the two quarters either side of the blind spot, while `Aft` as a SIX-arc name is the blind spot
itself and expands to nothing firable. Both sides have to answer that the same way and both do.

cases.why: the plain spelling, and the control that must be accepted
an all-round turret bears through every arc a weapon may fire through
an old ninety-degree side arc becomes the two sixty-degree arcs on that side
the OLD aft arc was ninety degrees and becomes the two quarters either side of the blind spot
the six-arc name spelled as the enum
THE DIVERGENCE: hyphenated is how a person writes it in a spreadsheet cell, and the client used to answer Fore
spaced, which the client already handled and the server did too
hyphenated and lower case at once
upper case with a hyphen, because a file is typed by hand
the last of the four hyphenated quarters
a name neither side recognises falls back rather than leaving a mount bearing nowhere
an empty cell is the same fallback

blindSpot.why: No weapon fires through the aft arc (rules-fidelity gap 3). An expansion that handed the blind spot back would put a mount there through the import door, so both sides are held to never producing it.
